## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and file path so you can open the source for full instructions when using a specific skill.
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use when the user asks how to build with OpenAI products or APIs and needs up-to-date official documentation with citations, help choosing the latest model for a use case, or explicit GPT-5.4 upgrade and prompt-upgrade guidance; prioritize OpenAI docs MCP tools, use bundled references only as helper context, and restrict any fallback browsing to official OpenAI domains. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, and baseline placeholders you can edit before publishing or testing. Use when Codex needs to create a new local plugin, add optional plugin structure, or generate or update repo-root `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + file path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, open its `SKILL.md`. Read only enough to follow the workflow.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the skill directory listed above first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, load only the specific files needed for the request; don't bulk-load everything.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Keep context small: summarize long sections instead of pasting them; only load extra files when needed.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions>

Build an 8-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation analyzing the top 20 trending GitHub repositories over the past 24 hours, targeting developer advocates, open-source community managers, and engineering leaders tracking AI tooling trends. The tone should be data-forward, analytical, and technically grounded.

The deck opens by establishing OSSInsight's credibility as a data source (10.6B+ GitHub events), then drills into the top trending repos ranked by score, examines language and category distributions, spotlights the emerging Claude Code ecosystem, compares community engagement metrics across repos, and closes with strategic takeaways on AI coding agent dominance.

For the "Top 5 Repos by Total Score" slide, use a horizontal bar chart or ranked table showing stars, forks, pushes, and PRs for each repo. For the "Language Distribution" slide, use a pie or donut chart reflecting the full breakdown (Python: 7, TypeScript: 4, HTML: 2, Rust: 2, Swift: 2, Shell: 1, Java: 1, Unspecified: 1). The "Category Breakdown" slide should use a stacked bar or treemap to visualize that ~70% of trending repos relate to AI coding assistance. The "Community Engagement" slide should use a scatter plot or grouped bar chart contrasting high- and low-engagement repos.

Do not fabricate any data not found in source_brief.md. All statistics, repo names, and metrics must come directly from the provided brief.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

# GitHub Trending Repos Snapshot: The Rise of AI Coding Agents and Claude Code Skills

## Source
https://ossinsight.io/

## About OSSInsight

OSSInsight is a free, real-time analytics platform that tracks over **10.6 billion GitHub events**. It provides deep insights into open-source repositories, developers, and organizations — covering stars, commits, pull requests, issues, contributors, and community health metrics. The platform ranks trending repositories using a composite **Total Score = Stars score + Forks score + Base score**.

The data below reflects the **top 20 trending repositories in the past 24 hours** across all programming languages.

## Top 20 Trending Repositories (Past 24 Hours)

| #20 | shareAI-lab/learn-claude-code | Nano Claude Code-like agent, built from 0 to 1 | 113 | 12 | 0 | 0 | TypeScript |

## Language Distribution

Across the top 20 trending repos, the programming language breakdown is:

- **Python**: 7 repos (35%)
- **TypeScript**: 4 repos (20%)
- **HTML**: 2 repos (10%)
- **Rust**: 2 repos (10%)
- **Swift**: 2 repos (10%)
- **Shell**: 1 repo (5%)
- **Java**: 1 repo (5%)
- **Unspecified**: 1 repo (5%)

Python's dominance reflects the AI/ML ecosystem's primary language, while TypeScript's strong showing aligns with developer tooling and agent UI frameworks.

## Thematic Categories

The trending repos cluster into clear thematic groups:

1. **AI Coding Agents & Skills** (~10 repos): hermes-agent, graphify, caveman, agent-skills, andrej-karpathy-skills, awesome-design-md, multica, DeepTutor, oh-my-codex, learn-claude-code
2. **Claude Code Ecosystem Tools** (~5 repos): claude-code-best-practice, claude-howto, cc-switch, caveman, learn-claude-code
3. **AI Infrastructure & Research** (~3 repos): VoxCPM, reverse-SynthID, opendataloader-pdf
4. **Developer Utilities** (~3 repos): InstantSpaceSwitcher, Recordly, rtk, clicky

Roughly **14 of the 20 repos** (70%) are directly related to AI coding agents, skills, or Claude Code tooling — a striking concentration.

## Community Engagement Patterns

Community activity is heavily concentrated at the top. NousResearch/hermes-agent alone accounts for **78 PRs** and **42 pushes**, dwarfing all other repos. multica-ai/multica is the second most active with 35 pushes and 7 PRs. Meanwhile, 8 of the 20 repos have **zero PRs**, suggesting many are early-stage or single-author projects riding initial hype.

## Key Findings

- **AI coding agents dominate GitHub trending**: 14 of the top 20 repos (70%) are AI coding agent tools, skills, or related resources — an unprecedented concentration in a single theme.
- **Claude Code has spawned a full ecosystem overnight**: At least 7 repos are specifically Claude Code skills, guides, best-practice collections, or multi-tool switchers, indicating rapid community formation around Anthropic's coding tool.
- **Python leads, but TypeScript is the runner-up**: Python powers 35% of trending repos (AI/ML core), while TypeScript (20%) drives agent UIs and developer experience layers.
- **Community engagement is top-heavy**: The #1 repo (hermes-agent) attracted 78 PRs in 24 hours; most repos below #8 show minimal collaborative activity, suggesting early-stage virality rather than mature community development.
- **Token efficiency is a hot sub-theme**: Multiple repos (caveman, rtk) focus specifically on reducing LLM token consumption — signaling cost-consciousness as AI coding tools scale.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from datetime import date

out_path = '/app/output/final_deck.pptx'
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Theme colors
BG = RGBColor(245, 247, 250)
PRIMARY = RGBColor(18, 52, 86)
ACCENT = RGBColor(0, 120, 212)
TEXT = RGBColor(32, 37, 43)
MUTED = RGBColor(90, 100, 110)

repos = [
    (1, 'NousResearch/hermes-agent', 1347, 101, 42, 78, 'Python'),
    (2, 'safishamsi/graphify', 742, 50, 6, 5, 'Python'),
    (3, 'VoltAgent/awesome-design-md', 615, 48, 1, 0, 'HTML'),
    (4, 'JuliusBrussee/caveman', 300, 11, 1, 1, 'Python'),
    (5, 'shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice', 304, 23, 0, 0, 'HTML'),
    (6, 'forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills', 267, 5, 0, 1, 'Unspecified'),
    (7, 'HKUDS/DeepTutor', 245, 23, 2, 0, 'Python'),
    (8, 'multica-ai/multica', 245, 29, 35, 7, 'TypeScript'),
    (9, 'opendataloader-project/opendataloader-pdf', 229, 17, 3, 1, 'Java'),
    (10, 'addyosmani/agent-skills', 191, 11, 0, 0, 'Shell'),
    (11, 'OpenBMB/VoxCPM', 171, 7, 0, 0, 'Python'),
    (12, 'aloshdenny/reverse-SynthID', 140, 13, 2, 1, 'Python'),
    (13, 'Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex', 159, 5, 10, 2, 'TypeScript'),
    (14, 'jurplel/InstantSpaceSwitcher', 132, 4, 2, 0, 'Swift'),
    (15, 'webadderall/Recordly', 144, 15, 1, 1, 'TypeScript'),
    (16, 'rtk-ai/rtk', 143, 7, 3, 5, 'Rust'),
    (17, 'luongnv89/claude-howto', 124, 12, 0, 0, 'Python'),
    (18, 'farion1231/cc-switch', 122, 4, 2, 2, 'Rust'),
    (19, 'farzaa/clicky', 132, 9, 0, 2, 'Swift'),
    (20, 'shareAI-lab/learn-claude-code', 113, 12, 0, 0, 'TypeScript'),
]

def add_bg(slide):
    fill = slide.background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = BG

def add_title(slide, title, subtitle=None):
    tbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.2), Inches(0.9))
    tf = tbox.text_frame
    tf.clear()
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = title
    run.font.size = Pt(30)
    run.font.bold = True
    run.font.color.rgb = PRIMARY
    if subtitle:
        p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
        p2.text = subtitle
        p2.font.size = Pt(15)
        p2.font.color.rgb = MUTED

# Slide 1: Title
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, 'GitHub Trending Repos Snapshot: The Rise of AI Coding Agents & Claude Code Skills',
          'OSSInsight dataset: 10.6B+ GitHub events | Top 20 trending repos in past 24 hours')
date_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(1.8), Inches(6), Inches(0.6))
date_box.text_frame.text = f'Date context: {date.today().isoformat()}'
date_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(16)
date_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TEXT

# Slide 2: platform overview
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6]); add_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, 'OSSInsight Tracks 10.6 Billion GitHub Events in Real Time')
metrics = [
    '10.6B+ GitHub events tracked',
    'Covers stars, commits, PRs, issues, reviews',
    'Real-time repository/developer/organization insights',
    'Trending rank uses composite score: Stars + Forks + Base score'
]
for i,m in enumerate(metrics):
    tb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.9), Inches(1.5+i*1.1), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.9))
    p = tb.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = f'• {m}'
    p.font.size = Pt(24 if i==0 else 20)
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT

# Slide 3: top 5 table
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6]); add_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, 'hermes-agent Leads with 1,347 Stars — Top 5 Repos by Total Score')
rows, cols = 6, 6
table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.4), Inches(12.3), Inches(4.8)).table
headers = ['Rank','Repository','Stars','Forks','Pushes','PRs']
for c,h in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0,c)
    cell.text = h
    cell.fill.solid(); cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = PRIMARY
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]; p.font.bold=True; p.font.size=Pt(14); p.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255)
for r,(rank,name,stars,forks,pushes,prs_count,lang) in enumerate(repos[:5], start=1):
    vals=[f'#{rank}',name,str(stars),str(forks),str(pushes),str(prs_count)]
    for c,v in enumerate(vals):
        cell=table.cell(r,c); cell.text=v
        p=cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]; p.font.size=Pt(13); p.font.color.rgb=TEXT
note = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(6.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
note.text_frame.text = 'Observation: #1 hermes-agent combines highest stars (1,347) with strongest collaboration (78 PRs, 42 pushes).'
note.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(13)
note.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = ACCENT

# Slide 4: language pie
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6]); add_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, "Python and TypeScript Dominate Trending Repos' Language Mix")
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
langs = ['Python','TypeScript','HTML','Rust','Swift','Shell','Java','Unspecified']
vals = [7,4,2,2,2,1,1,1]
chart_data.categories = langs
chart_data.add_series('Repos', vals)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.PIE, Inches(0.9), Inches(1.3), Inches(6.6), Inches(5.4), chart_data).chart
chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.RIGHT
chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
chart.plots[0].has_data_labels = True
slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(7.8), Inches(2.0), Inches(5.0), Inches(2.2)).text_frame.text = 'Python: 7/20 (35%)\nTypeScript: 4/20 (20%)\nOne repo has unspecified language.'

# Slide 5: category breakdown
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6]); add_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, '14 of 20 Trending Repos Are AI Coding Agent or Claude Code Projects')
cd = CategoryChartData(); cd.categories=['Top 20 repos']
cd.add_series('AI coding assistance related', [14])
cd.add_series('Other categories', [6])
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_STACKED, Inches(0.9), Inches(2.0), Inches(7.8), Inches(2.2), cd).chart
chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.BOTTOM
slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(9.0), Inches(1.8), Inches(3.9), Inches(3.2)).text_frame.text = 'Thematic groups:\n• AI Coding Agents & Skills (~10)\n• Claude Code Ecosystem Tools (~5)\n• AI Infra & Research (~3)\n• Developer Utilities (~3)\n\n~70% are AI-coding-assistance related.'

# Slide 6: claude ecosystem
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6]); add_bg(slide)
add_title(slide, 'Claude Code Spawns an Ecosystem: Skills, Guides, Switches, and Best Practices')
left = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.7), Inches(1.4), Inches(6.2), Inches(4.8)).text_frame
left.text = 'Core Claude Code Ecosystem Tools (5 repos):'
for item in ['shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice','luongnv89/claude-howto','farion1231/cc-switch','JuliusBrussee/caveman','shareAI-lab/learn-claude-code']:
    p = left.add_paragraph(); p.text='• '+item
right = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(7.0), Inches(1.4), Inches(5.7), Inches(4.8)).text_frame
right.text = 'Broader Claude Code-adjacent set (at least 7):'
for item in ['Includes all 5 core repos','Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex','addyosmani/agent-skills']:
    p = right.add_paragraph(); p.text='• '+item
